christians-reading-classics.title: Sherlock Holmes and Advent Classics, with Tim Larsen
christians-reading-classics.description: Why would a Sherlock Holmes mystery open a collection of Christmas stories? In “The Adventure of the Blue Carbuncle,” a battered hat and a Christmas goose lead Holmes to a jewel thief. The ending turns on forgiveness. Timothy Larsen, sometimes called Dr. Christmas, joins Nadya to read it as an Advent story. They talk about why so many Christmas tales make room for suffering and death, what Conan Doyle’s later life says about our hunger for more than reason, a defense of honest sentiment, and how a family can start reading aloud together this season. Timothy Larsen is McManus Professor of Christian Thought and professor of history at Wheaton College. He is the editor of Twelve Classic Christmas Stories: A Feast of Yuletide Tales (Moody Publishers) and The Oxford Handbook of Christmas .
